The simulation uses OpenFOAM reactingParcelFoam to model a 2D axisymmetric spray combustion case in a cylindrical chamber of length 0.2 m and diameter 0.1 m, with the axis of symmetry along the centerline and one radial direction resolved.
The computational mesh is a structured 2D axisymmetric wedge grid generated with blockMesh, containing 100 cells in the axial direction, 50 cells in the radial direction, and 1 cell in the angular direction.
The mesh is graded with a simpleGrading of approximately 0.4 in both axial and radial directions to concentrate cells near the centerline axis and the inlet face where the injector resides, coarsening toward the outlet and outer wall.
The inlet is a uniform co-flow of hot air with axial velocity U = (10, 0, 0) m/s, temperature T = 800 K, pressure p = 101325 Pa, and mass fractions Y_O2 = 0.233, Y_N2 = 0.767.
Turbulence at the inlet is specified using standard inletValue or kqR-type boundary conditions with 5% turbulence intensity and a length scale of 0.07 times the inlet diameter (0.007 m).
Liquid n-dodecane is injected via a cone spray model located at the center of the inlet face on the axis, with a mass flow rate of 0.002 kg/s and a droplet temperature of 300 K.
The droplet size distribution follows a Rosin-Rammler distribution with a mean diameter of 50 micrometers and a spread parameter q = 2.0.
The cone half-angle is set to 10 degrees and the number of parcels per injection time step is set to 50.
The Lagrangian parcel model uses the Ranz-Marshall heat and mass transfer model for droplet evaporation and the standard Schiller-Naumann drag model.
The gas-phase turbulence is modeled with the standard k-epsilon RAS model.
Wall boundaries use no-slip for velocity, fixed temperature T = 400 K, and standard k-epsilon wall functions (nutkWallFunction for k and nut, epsilonWallFunction for epsilon).
The outlet boundary uses a totalPressure type fixed at 101325 Pa for pressure and zeroGradient for all other fields (U, T, species, k, epsilon, nut).
The centerline axis boundary uses the OpenFOAM axis boundary condition type for all fields to enforce radial velocity equals zero and apply the axisymmetric geometric source terms.
Combustion is modeled with a two-step global reaction mechanism involving six gas-phase species: nC12H26, O2, N2, CO, H2, CO2, H2O, plus liquid nC12H26.
Reaction 1 (partial oxidation): C12H26 + 6 O2 produces 12 CO + 13 H2, with Arrhenius parameters Ea1 approximately 150 kJ/mol and pre-exponential factor A1 approximately 1e9.
Reaction 2 (complete oxidation): 12 CO + 13 H2 + 12.5 O2 produces 12 CO2 + 13 H2O, with Arrhenius parameters Ea2 approximately 200 kJ/mol and pre-exponential factor A2 approximately 1e10.
The reaction rate form is Arrhenius multiplied by the Eddy-Dissipation finite-rate combination as handled by default in reactingParcelFoam.
The thermophysical type for all gas-phase species is janaf, using standard JANAF polynomial coefficients for O2, N2, CO, CO2, H2, and H2O, plus coefficients for dodecane vapor sourced from standard JANAF or Burcat thermodynamic tables.
Liquid n-dodecane thermo properties use the standard OpenFOAM liquid thermo with heat of vaporization appropriate for dodecane.
The solver is reactingParcelFoam, coupling Eulerian gas-phase reacting flow with Lagrangian spray parcel tracking.
The simulation runs transiently from t = 0 to endTime = 0.05 seconds with an adjustable time step controlled by the Courant number, maxCo = 0.7, initial deltaT = 1e-6 s, and a safety cap of maxDeltaT = 1e-5 s.
Output is written every 0.001 seconds (50 snapshots total) in ASCII format with no purge.
The simulation captures spray development, droplet evaporation, mixing with the hot co-flow, ignition, and establishment of a quasi-steady diffusion flame within the short 0.2 m chamber.
